storage_model.ledger: Append-only payload-free events with SHA-256 content fingerprints and exact owner, subject, audience and purpose scope.
storage_model.content: Separately held canonical JSON blobs that can be removed on erasure without deleting the audit tombstone.
storage_model.authority: Receipt availability is derived from accepted scope, current content, expiry, correction and erasure. Delivery never grants authority.
storage_model.projection: A prepared projection binds exact receipt IDs and becomes stale when any dependency becomes unavailable.

invariants: Exact receipt replay is idempotent and byte-stable.
Conflicting replay under one receipt identity is held without mutation.
Owner, subject, audience and purpose mismatch fails closed.
Expired, corrected or erased receipts are unavailable.
Correction invalidates only receipts with matching dependencies and stales their projections.
Correction time cannot predate the receipt it invalidates.
Erasure removes content, keeps a payload-free tombstone and blocks silent subject revival.
Delivery can occur only while a receipt is available and cannot preserve authority after correction.
Exact projection retry remains idempotent after later truth changes.
Non-JSON and malformed runtime input cannot create state.
closed_scope: transaction isolation or concurrent database behavior
residual_risks: The caller-provided in-memory state is not authenticated against tampering.
Content erasure models deletion but not encrypted key destruction or backup convergence.
Correction invalidation is terminal in R5; governed revalidation and replacement lineage are not yet modeled.
The erasure tombstone blocks future subject content until an explicit new-consent lifecycle is designed.
No database transaction, row policy, concurrent writer or readback behavior is proven.
